messages:
Ivy (Docs): opened PR to refresh the Nimbus2 model card + model-catalog row. Key updates: explicit supported-hardware matrix, clarified streaming long-context (32k with KV cache and caveats), corrected quant compatibility table to use runtime labels, and swapped in a streaming SDK snippet that demonstrates fallback handling. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5058 please skim for customer-facing wording.

Ben (Runtime): thanks. Please use runtime labels in the compat table (nimbus2-q4_k_m, nimbus2-q8_0, nimbus2-fp16). Also add a short note that runtime will automatically fall back to the fp16 variant when q4/q8 kernels are unavailable on a host. That prevents a lot of support noise.

Eli (Bench): pasted benchmark runs in the PR comments: nimbus2-q4_k_m on T4: 60-85 tok/s (batch=1, seq=4096); on A10: 180-220 tok/s (batch=1, seq=4096). Numbers vary with prompt shape and cold starts. I'll attach the harness and docker tag for reproducibility. Recommend reporting ranges and including the exact run command in a hidden PR artifact.

Rosa (DevEx): updated the python + TS snippets to the streaming client and added detection for runtime_fallback metadata. Python snippet in the PR:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
for chunk in client.generate_stream(prompt, model='nimbus2-q4_k_m'):
    if chunk.meta.get('runtime_fallback'):
        print('\n[fallback to ' + chunk.meta.get('runtime_variant') + ']')
    print(chunk.text, end='')
```
Please confirm meta key names are accurate.

Ben (Runtime): meta key names look correct: runtime_fallback (bool) and runtime_variant (string). One small nit: show an explicit example of pinning to nimbus2-fp16 for Dedicated customers who want to avoid fallbacks.

Marta (PM): avoid marketing absolutes in the public docs. For throughput callout use a qualified sentence, e.g. "expected throughput: ~60-85 tok/s on T4 and ~180-220 tok/s on A10 (batch=1, seq=4096); measured with the canonical benchmark prompts." Also add a one-line rollback/canary note for Dedicated.

ci-bot: docs-ci/pr-check failed — markdown-lint: duplicate-anchor-id in supported-hardware table. See https://ci.redwood.dev/1401

Ivy (Docs): fixing anchors and switching the internal runtime link to the public runtime mapping page. Also added Marta's phrasing for throughput and the Dedicated rollback note. Re-requesting review.

Eli (Bench): added a sentence about batching: "batching can increase amortized throughput but increases p95 latency; see batching guidance." Attached the bench script as requested.

Rosa (DevEx): pushed a small JS parity example and an extra comment showing how the stream emits a metadata event before the first fallback chunk.

ci-bot: docs-ci/pr-check passed on second run :white_check_mark:

Ivy (Docs): thanks everyone. I'll merge in ~10m and post a short summary in #docs-release calling out the catalog change, fallback behavior, and bench caveats.
